articles.headline: China's Delivery Robots Are Learning to Tackle the Night Shift

It also means quieter roads, reduced pedestrian traffic, and lower congestion. Driverless vehicles eliminate the cost of a human: they don't need night shift wages, they don't get tired, and they don't need to be paid extra for driving in the rain.

articles.headline: Problems in 22 scientific fields had solutions hiding in plain sight. An AI has found them
articles.blurb: Borrowing an idea from one research discipline to solve a problem in another is an age-old scientific trick. However, such clever leaps are rare because researchers don't tend to spend their time researching fields outside of their expertise. AI can easily hop between fields. BootLoops is a harness that can spot and solve problems in seemingly unrelated fields that share the same mathematical structures at massive scale. Researchers recently released 36 preprints produced with BootLoops covering a wide range of topics, including figuring out the age of sunspots, analyzing government health policies, and attempting to decipher a mysterious medieval manuscript.

Coinbase then post-trained Qwen3.5-9B on its proprietary Onramp fraud dataset. articles.headline: “You didn't do it right”
articles.blurb: When OKRs don't work, how many times are you supposed to try again? WP Engine gave them four attempts, including paid training and coaching, and kept hearing that it wasn't doing them properly. What eventually worked was much smaller. One team picked a metric it cared about, set a loose goal, and followed it for a quarter before adding anything else. The metric also had to measure something the team could actually control, so people weren't being judged on a number their own work couldn't fix.

articles.headline: Your Churn Problem Started in the Comp Plan
articles.blurb: Your reps are hitting their targets, but a year later the customers are gone. One founder in this piece lost 30% of the previous year's new customers and wanted to know what was wrong. The answer starts with what reps get paid to sell. In a separate Airtable example, a birthday-calendar user counted as much toward the new-logo target as a team running a critical workflow. Airtable began scoring prospects against its best customers, giving reps smaller account lists and paying more for customers with room to grow.

articles.headline: Introducing Open Intelligent UI: the Open-Source Alternative to ChatGPT's Intelligent UI

Open Intelligent UI is compatible with any model and works with existing components. It runs generated code in an isolated iframe, and it can only load libraries from an approved list of CDNs.

articles.headline: Models as Insider Risks in the Super Intelligence Era
articles.blurb: We need to separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it. This means surrounding non-deterministic models with strong, deterministic system design, human controls, and reliable operating procedures, and establishing industry standards where existing ones are insufficient. Any sufficiently capable actor with access to important systems can make mistakes or be compromised. The architecture of containment and control must account for that.

Its rapid development demonstrates how AI coding tools could allow tiny teams to reproduce increasingly sophisticated professional software that previously required huge organizations to build. The development creates an ironic reversal for Adobe, whose own embrace of generative AI has faced criticism from creatives concerned about AI systems reproducing their work.

articles.headline: The New Big Ball of Mud: Why Agentic AI Systems Turn Fragile
articles.blurb: With AI making building nearly free, vibe architects without technical backgrounds grow agentic systems piecemeal into fragile "big balls of mud." Study participants kept throwaway drafts, bolted-on features, and let the AI patch files until they could no longer locate or recreate their own systems. Keeping global, local, and ambient context separate lets builders direct a rebuild instead of relying on the AI as sole navigator.

articles.headline: Handle Token Exceptions
articles.blurb: Hardcoded values become valid token exceptions only with a reason, a defined scope, an owner, and an end date. Without a date, they're permanent technical debt. Valid cases include time-boxed campaigns, tokens awaiting release, and urgent accessibility fixes. A register tracks each exception's location, value, reason, approver, and expiration date, and when the date arrives, it's promoted to a token or removed.

articles.headline: Designing Michelangelus
articles.blurb: Michelangelus is a new serif typeface inspired by Michelangelo's handwritten manuscripts, architectural work, and carved inscriptions, created by Studiogusto for the 400th anniversary of the consecration of St. Peter's Basilica. Rather than reproducing his handwriting literally, the designers studied its rhythm, spacing, proportions, distinctive forms, and hidden structural order, even spending a week refining the lowercase “g” derived from his signature. The resulting family contains more than 2,000 glyphs across regular, italic, bold, and bold italic styles and will become available across Microsoft 365 later this year.

articles.headline: On giving fluid interfaces an anchor
articles.blurb: Interfaces that continuously reshape themselves in response to context, AI, or user intent risk becoming difficult to understand because people lose the stable landmarks they use to build a mental model of a product. Keeping frequently used action buttons anchored while content expands gives users a predictable place to click or tap as the interface changes. Fluid interfaces therefore work best when adaptability is balanced with enough permanence for users to understand where they are, what changed, and how to get back.

articles.headline: Why Icon Consistency is Harder Than It Looks

The AI-native finance organization is smaller and higher leverage, with continuous forecasting, finance engineers, agent-driven workflows, and stronger audit controls, while the CFO focuses more on designing what people versus software should do and less on manually collecting and reconciling data.

articles.headline: Where will banks make money if it isn't from payments?
articles.blurb: AI agents and programmable money are pushing financial value away from transaction processing and toward orchestration, identity, liquidity, compliance, and software. McKinsey estimates agentic AI could put $75 billion to $160 billion of payments revenue at risk by 2030, while Capgemini says $230 billion is already exposed across areas like FX spreads, correspondent fees, and float income. The emerging battleground is increasingly about who controls the intelligence that decides how money moves, whether that is a bank, fintech, software platform, or AI agent.

The AFP did not name the defendants, but KrebsOnSecurity learned the 21-year-old suspect's real identity in June, and has been communicating with him ever since. It is expected to strengthen to a category 2 hurricane as it approaches the US’s northern Gulf coast on Friday, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). As a result of the strong El Niño, it has been a notably quiet Atlantic hurricane season.
